newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei ends down more than 3% on tax report.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei ends down more than 3% on tax report.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market's key Nikkei index ended down more than three percent on Monday, as losses accelerated late in the session on a domestic media report that Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka has hinted at the possibility of another rise in the sales tax following the planned two percentage point increase in April, brokers said.
The 225-share Nikkei average fell 589.34 points or 3.16 percent to 18,043.82. Its June futures tumbled 500 points to 18,090.

"The market had been supported in the morning session by reports on government plans to boost land liquidity," said Kunihiro Hatae, Tokyo Securities Co Ltd general manager. "But then the tax hike reports came along to send the indices downhill."
Jiji news agency quoted Mitsuzuka as saying: "I would not deny a tax increase during the long course of managing the nation. Such a case is possible."
